analysis:
The PR is documentation-only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, docs/architecture/inference.md). I found no changed enforcement code, so there is no concrete regression. The source change the docs describe is new retention of free 64 MiB paged-KV segments.

What the docs now say:
- Free segments from a released row are parked per pool, up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8). They sit outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. The next same-size admission reinstalls them (inference.md ~1095-1115).
- New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages.
- Parked backing is dropped on a refused admission, on a process-wide release request (memory pressure, a refused charge, a load gate or preload check), and after 30 s of engine idleness.
- Load gates and pre-accept paths now call releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad before evicting or refusing (hardware-support.md lines 298-299, 361-395; inference.md ~404-413). They give no eviction credit for segments still parked after the release, which is fail-safe for the memory ledger.
- An idle-cache sweep runs through WholeMacServiceBudget.performIfIdle.
- Env kill switches are DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0 and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0.

Open questions for later review, with no code supplied to confirm or refute them:
1. Parked segments reused for a different request or consumer may carry prior-tenant KV bytes (A-001, T-028). The docs say only new segments are zero-fill-on-demand, and do not say whether reinstalled segments are cleared or whether attention only reads positions that have been written. This is the main data-exposure question. If reinstalled segments are not cleared, the T-028 residual-data language may need an update.
2. Parked memory is uncharged to the ledger, up to 2 GiB per pool and per engine. The docs claim it is released under pressure and counted via U (the allocator reading). Confirm that this holds for multi-engine availability and does not enable an OOM or DoS (T-010, T-029).
3. The retention path interacts with the prefix cache and SSD staging reservations (T-041). Confirm there is no cache-scope leakage through reinstalled segments.

No trust-boundary, authorization or attestation behavior changes in the supplied text.
